description: A vs B: two panels whose points appear in turns, and optionally a winner.
useWhen: Two options exist at the same time and the viewer has to tell them apart.

long.title: Synchronous requests versus asynchronous messages between two services

left.label: Synchronous requests
points: The caller waits until the other service answers the request
Simple to follow from a single trace on a single screen
A slow dependency quickly slows down everything behind it
Failures show up immediately, right where they happened
Easy to reason about when there are only a few services

right.label: Asynchronous messages
points: The caller leaves a message on a queue and carries on working
Harder to follow: one action is spread over several services
A slow consumer only makes the queue grow for a little while
Failures can stay hidden until the dead letter queue fills up
Scales better when many consumers share the same workload

captions: Both talk between services, but they fail in very different ways.
If the user does not need the answer now, prefer messages.
